                [32m'  example `"order[line_items]"`, `"order[line_items][0][modifiers]"` or\n'[39m +

                [32m'  depth must work.\n'[39m +
                [32m"- `new_order_form/0` builds a create form for `Catering.Orders.Order`'s `:place` action;\n"[39m +
                [32m'  `edit_order_form/1` builds an update form for the `:revise` action of the order with that id.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- The third argument of `change/3` and `add_nested/3` is a keyword list that must be forwarded\n'[39m +

                [32m'  restrict validation to touched fields, seed the new nested form with parameters, insert it at\n'[39m +
                [32m'  the front of the list, or give it a non-default action type. Both functions must also be\n'[39m +
                [32m'  callable at the lower arity with the options defaulting to `[]`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `reorder/3` and `move/3` change the visible order **and** the order that will be submitted: the\n'[39m +
                [32m'  reordered children must appear in the new order in `submitted_params/1`, they must be renamed to\n'[39m +
                [32m'  their new indices, and `save/2` must persist the new order. `move/3` at either boundary of a list\n'[39m +
                [32m'  is a no-op.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `edit_order_form/1` must present nested children in ascending stored `position`, independently of\n'[39m +
                [32m'  the order the storage engine happens to return them in.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Removing a nested form from an edit form and saving must destroy exactly that stored record,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  leaving unrelated records untouched.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `save/2` takes the form and either a parameter map (which must be validated into the form before\n'[39m +
                [32m'  submitting) or `nil` (submit what the form already holds). On success it returns\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `{:ok, order}` where `order` is the persisted `Catering.Orders.Order` struct with `customer`,\n'[39m +
                [32m"  `line_items` and each line item's `modifiers` already loaded, and with the line items and the\n"[39m +
                [32m'  modifiers in ascending `position`. On failure it returns `{:error, form}` where `form` is the\n'[39m +
                [32m'  re-usable `%AshPhoenix.Form{}` carrying the errors, and nothing has been written.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `hidden_inputs/2` returns a `%{String.t() => String.t()}` map: every hidden input key (including\n'[39m +
                [32m'  the form-type marker `_form_type`, the touched-field marker `_touched`, the primary key of an\n'[39m +
                [32m'  existing record, and the union member marker `_union_type`) mapped to its string value.\n'[39m +

                [32m'  without errors must be absent from the map.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `raw_error_list/2` returns the errors of the form at `path` as a list of\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `{field :: atom(), message :: String.t(), vars :: keyword()}` tuples with the message left\n'[39m +
                [32m'  untranslated (substitution variables not interpolated), sorted ascending by field name and then\n'[39m +
                [32m'  by message.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `serialize/1` returns, for the form it is given and recursively for every nested form, a map with\n'[39m +
                [32m'  exactly these string keys:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"name"` — the form\'s HTML name.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"id"` — the form\'s HTML id.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"type"` — `"create"`, `"update"` or `"read"`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"resource"` — the form\'s resource module rendered with `inspect/1`, e.g.\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `"Catering.Orders.LineItem"`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"valid"` — the form\'s validity as a boolean.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"hidden"` — the same map as `hidden_inputs/2` would return for this form, but **without** the\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `_touched` entry.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"values"` — a map from field name to the form\'s current value for that field, rendered with\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `to_string/1`, or `nil` when the value is `nil`. The fields are, per resource:\n'[39m +

                    [32m'# Nested Forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"Make sure you're familiar with the basics of `AshPhoenix.Form` before reading this guide.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'When we talk about "nested" or "related" forms, we mean sets of form inputs\n'[39m +
                    [32m'that are for resource actions for related or embedded resources.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example, you might have a form for creating a "business" that can also\n'[39m +
                    [32m'include multiple "locations". In some cases, you may have buttons to add or \n'[39m +
                    [32m'remove from a list of nested forms, you may be able to drag and drop to reorder\n'[39m +
                    [32m'forms, etc. In other cases, the form may just be for one related thing, think\n'[39m +
                    [32m'a form for updating a "user" that also contains inputs for its associated "profile".\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Defining the structure\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Inferring from the action\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`AshPhoenix.Form` automatically infers what "nested forms" are available, based on introspecting actions\n'[39m +
                    [32m'which use `change manage_relationship`. For example, in the following action:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# on a `MyApp.Operations.Business` resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'create :create do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  accept [:name]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  argument :locations, {:array, :map}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  change manage_relationship(:locations, type: :create)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'With this action, you could submit an input like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'%{name: "Wally World", locations: [%{name: "HQ", address: "1 hq street"}]}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"`AshPhoenix.Form` will look at the action, allowing you to use `Phoenix`'s\n"[39m +
                    [32m'`<.inputs_for` component for `locations`. Here is what it might look like in\n'[39m +
                    [32m'practice:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To turn this automatic behavior off, you can specify `forms: [auto?: false]` \n'[39m +
                    [32m'when creating the form.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Manually defining nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can manually specify nested form configurations using the `forms` option.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'AshPhoenix.Form.for_create(\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  MyApp.Operations.Business, \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  :create, \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  forms: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    locations: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      type: :list,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      resource: MyApp.Operations.Location,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      create_action: :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m')\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You should prefer to use the automatic form definition wherever possible,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'but this exists as an escape hatch to customize configuration.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Updating existing data\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You should be sure to load any relationships that are necessary for your\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`manage_relationship`s when you want to update the nested items. \n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example, if the form above was for an update action,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'you may want to allow updating the existing locations all in a single form.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`AshPhoenix.Form` will show a form for each existing location, but only if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'the locations are loaded on the business already. For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'business = Ash.load!(business, :locations)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'form = AshPhoenix.Form.for_update(business, :update)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### Not using tailwind? {: .warning}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> If you\'re not using tailwind, you\'ll need to replace `class="hidden"`\n'[39m +
                    [32m"> in the examples below with something else. In standard HTML, you'd do\n"[39m +
                    [32m"> `<input .... hidden />`. As long as the checkbox is hidden, you're good!\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Adding nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'There are two ways to add nested forms.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### The `_add_*` checkbox\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      type="checkbox"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      name={"#{@form.name}[_add_locations]"}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      value="end"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      class="hidden"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.icon name="hero-plus" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This checkbox, when checked, will add a parameter like `form[_add_locations]=end`. \n'[39m +
                    [32m'When `AshPhoenix.Form` is handling nested forms, it will see that and append an empty\n'[39m +
                    [32m'form at the end. Valid values are `"start"`, `"end"` and an index, i.e `"3"`, in which\n'[39m +
                    [32m'case the new form will be inserted at that index.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### But the checkbox is hidden, what gives? {: .info}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m"> If you're anything like me, the label + checkbox combo above may confuse you \n"[39m +
                    [32m'> at first sight. When you have a checkbox inside of a label, clicking on the label\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> [counts as clicking the checkbox itself](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#providing_a_bigger_hit_area_for_your_checkboxes)!\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `AshPhoenix.Form.add_form`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"In some cases, you may want to add a form either in a way that can't be triggered by a checkbox\n"[39m +
                    [32m'or that requires some additional data (like non-empty starting params). In those cases,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'you can use a button and a `handle_event` For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.button type="button" phx-click="add-form" phx-value-path={@form.name <> "[locations]"}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.icon name="hero-plus" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.button>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### whats with `@form.name <> "[locations]"` {: .info}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> By always using a path "relative" to the root form, we can handle cases where we are\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> adding a form to a multiply-nested form. So the path could be somethign like\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> locations[0][addresses][1]. The event handler has to know exactly where we are adding\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> a form. In the example above, we *could* just say `add_form(form, :locations)`. It would\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> be simpler, but we want to highlight how to work with potentially deeply nested data.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'def handle_event("add-form", %{"path" => path}, socket) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  form = AshPhoenix.Form.add_form(socket.assigns.form, path, params: %{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    address: "Put your address here!"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Removing nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Just like adding nested forms, there are two ways to *remove* nested forms.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using the `_drop_*` checkbox\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'The `_drop_*` checkbox uses checkboxes which add form indices to a list that should\n'[39m +
                    [32m'be *removed* from the list. For example, given the following:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        type="checkbox"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        name={"#{@form.name}[_drop_locations][]"}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        value={location.index}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        class="hidden"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <.icon name="hero-x-mark" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'When the checkbox is checked, the server sees:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'%{"form" => %{"_drop_locations" => ["0"]}}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'We use this information to automatically remove the item at that index on validate.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using `AshPhoenix.Form.remove_form`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Just like adding forms, there is a manual way to remove forms. In this case\n'[39m +
                    [32m'we pass the full path to the form being removed.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.button type="button" phx-click="remove-form" phx-value-path={location.name}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <.icon name="hero-x-mark" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </.button>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'def handle_event("remove-form", %{"path" => path}, socket) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  form = AshPhoenix.Form.remove_form(socket.assigns.form, path)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Sorting nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Just like adding and removing forms, there are two ways to *sort* nested forms too!\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using `_sort_*` checkboxes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This method is useful when combined with something like [`sortable.js`](https://sortablejs.github.io/Sortable/) \n'[39m +
                    [32m'to allow for dragging and dropping on the front end.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### the `order_is_key` option {: .info}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> If you are working with a sorted relationship, you will likely want to couple it\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> with the `order_is_key` option of `managed_relationships`. This writes the order\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> of items in the list of inputs into each input, as if it was provided as an input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> `change manage_relationship(:locations, type: :direct_control, order_is_key: :position)`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> In the above example, if you provided a list of inputs like\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> `[%{address: "foo"}, %{address: "bar"}]`, it would first be converted into\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> `[%{address: "foo, order: 0}, %{address: "bar", order: 1}]` before being\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> processed.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Lets say you had the following `Sortable` hook in your `app.js`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```js\n'[39m +
                    [32m'import Sortable from "sortablejs"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export const Sortable = {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  mounted() {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    new Sortable(this.el, {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      animation: 150,\n'[39m +
                    [32m`      draggable: '[data-sortable="true"]',\n`[39m +
                    [32m'      ghostClass: "bg-yellow-100",\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      dragClass: "shadow-2xl",\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      onEnd: (evt) => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        this.el.closest("form").querySelector("input").dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    })\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'let Hooks = {}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Hooks.Sortable = Sortable\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You could use the `_sort_*` checkbox in each nested form like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <div id="location-list" phx-hook="Sortable">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <div data-sortable="true">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          type="hidden"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          name={"#{@form.name}[_sort_locations][]"}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          value={location_form.index}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      </div>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"In this case you'd drag the entire div. `sortable.js` supports all kinds of useful features,\n"[39m +
                    [32m'like drag handles. See [their docs](https://sortablejs.github.io/Sortable/) for more. \n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Now, lets say you were to drag the second form above the first form, the server would see the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'params as:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'%{"form" => %{"_sort_locations" => ["1", "0"]}}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`AshPhoenix.Form` would then sort the nested forms accordingly.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using `AshPhoenix.Form.sort_forms/3`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'The manual way is using  `AshPhoenix.Form.sort_forms/3`. This can be used\n'[39m +
                    [32m'to move a specific element up or down, or to sort all forms. `sortable.js`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'can be used in such a way that it provides the full sorting b'[39m... 3783 more characters,
                  isTruncated: [33mfalse[39m
                }

                    [32m'  <.icon name="hero-plus" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.button>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'In your LiveView:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'def handle_event("add-form", %{"path" => path}, socket) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  form = AshPhoenix.Form.add_form(socket.assigns.form, path)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}\n'[39m +

                    [32m'def handle_event("remove-form", %{"path" => path}, socket) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  form = AshPhoenix.Form.remove_form(socket.assigns.form, path)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}\n'[39m +

                    [32m'```'[39m,

              toolName: [32m'readFile'[39m,
              output: {
                type: [32m'json'[39m,
                value: {
                  content: [32m'<!--\n'[39m +
                    [32m'SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2020 Zach Daniel\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n'[39m +
                    [32m'-->\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Nested Forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"Make sure you're familiar with the basics of `AshPhoenix.Form` before reading this guide.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'When we talk about "nested" or "related" forms, we mean sets of form inputs\n'[39m +
                    [32m'that are for resource actions for related or embedded resources.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example, you might have a form for creating a "business" that can also\n'[39m +
                    [32m'include multiple "locations". In some cases, you may have buttons to add or \n'[39m +
                    [32m'remove from a list of nested forms, you may be able to drag and drop to reorder\n'[39m +
                    [32m'forms, etc. In other cases, the form may just be for one related thing, think\n'[39m +
                    [32m'a form for updating a "user" that also contains inputs for its associated "profile".\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Defining the structure\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Inferring from the action\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`AshPhoenix.Form` automatically infers what "nested forms" are available, based on introspecting actions\n'[39m +
                    [32m'which use `change manage_relationship`. For example, in the following action:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# on a `MyApp.Operations.Business` resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'create :create do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  accept [:name]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  argument :locations, {:array, :map}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  change manage_relationship(:locations, type: :create)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'With this action, you could submit an input like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'%{name: "Wally World", locations: [%{name: "HQ", address: "1 hq street"}]}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"`AshPhoenix.Form` will look at the action, allowing you to use `Phoenix`'s\n"[39m +
                    [32m'`<.inputs_for` component for `locations`. Here is what it might look like in\n'[39m +
                    [32m'practice:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To turn this automatic behavior off, you can specify `forms: [auto?: false]` \n'[39m +
                    [32m'when creating the form.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Manually defining nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can manually specify nested form configurations using the `forms` option.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'AshPhoenix.Form.for_create(\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  MyApp.Operations.Business, \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  :create, \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  forms: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    locations: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      type: :list,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      resource: MyApp.Operations.Location,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      create_action: :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m')\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You should prefer to use the automatic form definition wherever possible,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'but this exists as an escape hatch to customize configuration.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Updating existing data\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You should be sure to load any relationships that are necessary for your\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`manage_relationship`s when you want to update the nested items. \n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example, if the form above was for an update action,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'you may want to allow updating the existing locations all in a single form.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`AshPhoenix.Form` will show a form for each existing location, but only if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'the locations are loaded on the business already. For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'business = Ash.load!(business, :locations)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'form = AshPhoenix.Form.for_update(business, :update)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### Not using tailwind? {: .warning}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> If you\'re not using tailwind, you\'ll need to replace `class="hidden"`\n'[39m +
                    [32m"> in the examples below with something else. In standard HTML, you'd do\n"[39m +
                    [32m"> `<input .... hidden />`. As long as the checkbox is hidden, you're good!\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Adding nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'There are two ways to add nested forms.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### The `_add_*` checkbox\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      type="checkbox"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      name={"#{@form.name}[_add_locations]"}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      value="end"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      class="hidden"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.icon name="hero-plus" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This checkbox, when checked, will add a parameter like `form[_add_locations]=end`. \n'[39m +
                    [32m'When `AshPhoenix.Form` is handling nested forms, it will see that and append an empty\n'[39m +
                    [32m'form at the end. Valid values are `"start"`, `"end"` and an index, i.e `"3"`, in which\n'[39m +
                    [32m'case the new form will be inserted at that index.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### But the checkbox is hidden, what gives? {: .info}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m"> If you're anything like me, the label + checkbox combo above may confuse you \n"[39m +
                    [32m'> at first sight. When you have a checkbox inside of a label, clicking on the label\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> [counts as clicking the checkbox itself](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#providing_a_bigger_hit_area_for_your_checkboxes)!\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `AshPhoenix.Form.add_form`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"In some cases, you may want to add a form either in a way that can't be triggered by a checkbox\n"[39m +
                    [32m'or that requires some additional data (like non-empty starting params). In those cases,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'you can use a button and a `handle_event` For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.button type="button" phx-click="add-form" phx-value-path={@form.name <> "[locations]"}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.icon name="hero-plus" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.button>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### whats with `@form.name <> "[locations]"` {: .info}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> By always using a path "relative" to the root form, we can handle cases where we are\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> adding a form to a multiply-nested form. So the path could be somethign like\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> locations[0][addresses][1]. The event handler has to know exactly where we are adding\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> a form. In the example above, we *could* just say `add_form(form, :locations)`. It would\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> be simpler, but we want to highlight how to work with potentially deeply nested data.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'def handle_event("add-form", %{"path" => path}, socket) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  form = AshPhoenix.Form.add_form(socket.assigns.form, path, params: %{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    address: "Put your address here!"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Removing nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Just like adding nested forms, there are two ways to *remove* nested forms.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using the `_drop_*` checkbox\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'The `_drop_*` checkbox uses checkboxes which add form indices to a list that should\n'[39m +
                    [32m'be *removed* from the list. For example, given the following:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        type="checkbox"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        name={"#{@form.name}[_drop_locations][]"}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        value={location.index}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        class="hidden"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <.icon name="hero-x-mark" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'When the checkbox is checked, the server sees:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +

                    [32m'# Nested Forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"Make sure you're familiar with the basics of `AshPhoenix.Form` before reading this guide.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'When we talk about "nested" or "related" forms, we mean sets of form inputs\n'[39m +
                    [32m'that are for resource actions for related or embedded resources.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example, you might have a form for creating a "business" that can also\n'[39m +
                    [32m'include multiple "locations". In some cases, you may have buttons to add or \n'[39m +
                    [32m'remove from a list of nested forms, you may be able to drag and drop to reorder\n'[39m +
                    [32m'forms, etc. In other cases, the form may just be for one related thing, think\n'[39m +
                    [32m'a form for updating a "user" that also contains inputs for its associated "profile".\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Defining the structure\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Inferring from the action\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`AshPhoenix.Form` automatically infers what "nested forms" are available, based on introspecting actions\n'[39m +
                    [32m'which use `change manage_relationship`. For example, in the following action:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# on a `MyApp.Operations.Business` resource\n'[39m +
                    [32m'create :create do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  accept [:name]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  argument :locations, {:array, :map}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  change manage_relationship(:locations, type: :create)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'With this action, you could submit an input like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'%{name: "Wally World", locations: [%{name: "HQ", address: "1 hq street"}]}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"`AshPhoenix.Form` will look at the action, allowing you to use `Phoenix`'s\n"[39m +
                    [32m'`<.inputs_for` component for `locations`. Here is what it might look like in\n'[39m +
                    [32m'practice:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To turn this automatic behavior off, you can specify `forms: [auto?: false]` \n'[39m +
                    [32m'when creating the form.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Manually defining nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can manually specify nested form configurations using the `forms` option.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'AshPhoenix.Form.for_create(\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  MyApp.Operations.Business, \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  :create, \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  forms: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    locations: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      type: :list,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      resource: MyApp.Operations.Location,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      create_action: :create\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ]\n'[39m +
                    [32m')\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You should prefer to use the automatic form definition wherever possible,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'but this exists as an escape hatch to customize configuration.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Updating existing data\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You should be sure to load any relationships that are necessary for your\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`manage_relationship`s when you want to update the nested items. \n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example, if the form above was for an update action,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'you may want to allow updating the existing locations all in a single form.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`AshPhoenix.Form` will show a form for each existing location, but only if\n'[39m +
                    [32m'the locations are loaded on the business already. For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'business = Ash.load!(business, :locations)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'form = AshPhoenix.Form.for_update(business, :update)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### Not using tailwind? {: .warning}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> If you\'re not using tailwind, you\'ll need to replace `class="hidden"`\n'[39m +
                    [32m"> in the examples below with something else. In standard HTML, you'd do\n"[39m +
                    [32m"> `<input .... hidden />`. As long as the checkbox is hidden, you're good!\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Adding nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'There are two ways to add nested forms.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### The `_add_*` checkbox\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      type="checkbox"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      name={"#{@form.name}[_add_locations]"}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      value="end"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      class="hidden"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.icon name="hero-plus" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This checkbox, when checked, will add a parameter like `form[_add_locations]=end`. \n'[39m +
                    [32m'When `AshPhoenix.Form` is handling nested forms, it will see that and append an empty\n'[39m +
                    [32m'form at the end. Valid values are `"start"`, `"end"` and an index, i.e `"3"`, in which\n'[39m +
                    [32m'case the new form will be inserted at that index.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### But the checkbox is hidden, what gives? {: .info}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m"> If you're anything like me, the label + checkbox combo above may confuse you \n"[39m +
                    [32m'> at first sight. When you have a checkbox inside of a label, clicking on the label\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> [counts as clicking the checkbox itself](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#providing_a_bigger_hit_area_for_your_checkboxes)!\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### `AshPhoenix.Form.add_form`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"In some cases, you may want to add a form either in a way that can't be triggered by a checkbox\n"[39m +
                    [32m'or that requires some additional data (like non-empty starting params). In those cases,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'you can use a button and a `handle_event` For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.button type="button" phx-click="add-form" phx-value-path={@form.name <> "[locations]"}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.icon name="hero-plus" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.button>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### whats with `@form.name <> "[locations]"` {: .info}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> By always using a path "relative" to the root form, we can handle cases where we are\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> adding a form to a multiply-nested form. So the path could be somethign like\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> locations[0][addresses][1]. The event handler has to know exactly where we are adding\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> a form. In the example above, we *could* just say `add_form(form, :locations)`. It would\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> be simpler, but we want to highlight how to work with potentially deeply nested data.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'def handle_event("add-form", %{"path" => path}, socket) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  form = AshPhoenix.Form.add_form(socket.assigns.form, path, params: %{\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    address: "Put your address here!"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  })\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Removing nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Just like adding nested forms, there are two ways to *remove* nested forms.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using the `_drop_*` checkbox\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'The `_drop_*` checkbox uses checkboxes which add form indices to a list that should\n'[39m +
                    [32m'be *removed* from the list. For example, given the following:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        type="checkbox"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        name={"#{@form.name}[_drop_locations][]"}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        value={location.index}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        class="hidden"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <.icon name="hero-x-mark" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </label>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'When the checkbox is checked, the server sees:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'%{"form" => %{"_drop_locations" => ["0"]}}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'We use this information to automatically remove the item at that index on validate.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using `AshPhoenix.Form.remove_form`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Just like adding forms, there is a manual way to remove forms. In this case\n'[39m +
                    [32m'we pass the full path to the form being removed.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.button type="button" phx-click="remove-form" phx-value-path={location.name}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <.icon name="hero-x-mark" />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </.button>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'def handle_event("remove-form", %{"path" => path}, socket) do\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  form = AshPhoenix.Form.remove_form(socket.assigns.form, path)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Sorting nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Just like adding and removing forms, there are two ways to *sort* nested forms too!\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using `_sort_*` checkboxes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This method is useful when combined with something like [`sortable.js`](https://sortablejs.github.io/Sortable/) \n'[39m +
                    [32m'to allow for dragging and dropping on the front end.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> ### the `order_is_key` option {: .info}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> If you are working with a sorted relationship, you will likely want to couple it\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> with the `order_is_key` option of `managed_relationships`. This writes the order\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> of items in the list of inputs into each input, as if it was provided as an input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> `change manage_relationship(:locations, type: :direct_control, order_is_key: :position)`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> In the above example, if you provided a list of inputs like\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> `[%{address: "foo"}, %{address: "bar"}]`, it would first be converted into\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> `[%{address: "foo, order: 0}, %{address: "bar", order: 1}]` before being\n'[39m +
                    [32m'> processed.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Lets say you had the following `Sortable` hook in your `app.js`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```js\n'[39m +
                    [32m'import Sortable from "sortablejs"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export const Sortable = {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  mounted() {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    new Sortable(this.el, {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      animation: 150,\n'[39m +
                    [32m`      draggable: '[data-sortable="true"]',\n`[39m +
                    [32m'      ghostClass: "bg-yellow-100",\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      dragClass: "shadow-2xl",\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      onEnd: (evt) => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        this.el.closest("form").querySelector("input").dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    })\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'...\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'let Hooks = {}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Hooks.Sortable = Sortable\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You could use the `_sort_*` checkbox in each nested form like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```heex\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<.simple_form for={@form} phx-change="validate" phx-submit="submit">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <.input field={@form[:email]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  <div id="location-list" phx-hook="Sortable">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <.inputs_for :let={location} field={@form[:locations]}>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <div data-sortable="true">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <input\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          type="hidden"\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          name={"#{@form.name}[_sort_locations][]"}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          value={location_form.index}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <.input field={location[:name]} />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      </div>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"In this case you'd drag the entire div. `sortable.js` supports all kinds of useful features,\n"[39m +
                    [32m'like drag handles. See [their docs](https://sortablejs.github.io/Sortable/) for more. \n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Now, lets say you were to drag the second form above the first form, the server would see the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'params as:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```elixir\n'[39m +
                    [32m'%{"form" => %{"_sort_locations" => ["1", "0"]}}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'`AshPhoenix.Form` would then sort the nested forms accordingly.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using `AshPhoenix.Form.sort_forms/3`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'The manual way is using  `AshPhoenix.Form.sort_forms/3`. This can be used\n'[39m +
                    [32m'to move a specific element up or down, or to sort all forms. `sortable.js`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'can be used in such a way that it provides the full sorting b'[39m... 3783 more characters,

                [32m'  `fulfillment` (a tagged union whose members are the embedded resources\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `Catering.Orders.CourierDrop` and `Catering.Orders.CounterPickup`); a `belongs_to :customer`\n'[39m +
                [32m'  and a `has_many :line_items`. Its create action is `:place` and its update action is `:revise`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `Catering.Orders.LineItem` — `dish` (string, required), `quantity` (integer, must be positive),\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `position` (integer); `belongs_to :order`, `has_many :modifiers`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `Catering.Orders.Modifier` — `label` (string, required), `surcharge_cents` (integer, must not be\n'[39m +
                [32m'  negative), `position` (integer); `belongs_to :line_item`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `Catering.Orders.Customer` — `name` and `email` (both strings, required).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The `:place` and `:revise` actions already manage the whole `Order -> LineItem -> Modifier`\n'[39m +
                [32m'graph, the embedded delivery windows, the fulfillment union and the customer (which may either be\n'[39m +
                [32m'created inline from its attributes or matched to an already stored customer) from a single set of\n'[39m +
                [32m"submitted parameters, and they derive each child's `position` from the order in which the children\n"[39m +
                [32m'are submitted.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'The LiveView layer that will consume this is not part of this task: everything must be reachable\n'[39m +
                [32m'through plain function calls, with no HTTP server and no browser.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'Create `Catering.Forms`, a single facade module that a LiveView would use to build, mutate,\n'[39m +
                [32m'inspect and submit the whole nested order form. It must expose exactly these functions:\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'1. `new_order_form/0` — a blank create form for the order graph.\n'[39m +
                [32m'2. `edit_order_form/1` — takes an order id and returns an update form for the stored order,\n'[39m +
                [32m'   including nested forms for its existing line items and their modifiers.\n'[39m +
                [32m'3. `to_phoenix_form/1` — the `%Phoenix.HTML.Form{}` for a form.\n'[39m +
                [32m'4. `change/2` and `change/3` — revalidate a form against a fresh parameter map, with an optional\n'[39m +
                [32m'   keyword list of validation options.\n'[39m +
                [32m'5. `add_nested/2` and `add_nested/3` — add a nested form at a path, with an optional keyword list\n'[39m +
                [32m'   of options.\n'[39m +
                [32m'6. `remove_nested/2` — remove the nested form at a path.\n'[39m +
                [32m'7. `reorder/3` — reorder the nested list at a path, given the new ordering as a list of the\n'[39m +
                [32m'   current zero-based indices.\n'[39m +
                [32m'8. `move/3` — move the single nested form at a path one slot earlier (`:up`) or later (`:down`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'9. `submitted_params/1` — the parameter map that would be sent to the underlying action.\n'[39m +
                [32m'10. `hidden_inputs/2` — the hidden inputs required to render the form at a path.\n'[39m +
                [32m'11. `error_map/1` — the user-facing errors of the whole form tree.\n'[39m +
                [32m'12. `raw_error_list/2` — the untranslated errors of the form at a path.\n'[39m +
                [32m'13. `serialize/1` — a deterministic, plain-data snapshot of the whole form tree.\n'[39m +
                [32m'14. `save/2` — submit the form and persist the whole graph.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Project path: `/home/user/catering`. Write the module to\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `/home/user/catering/lib/catering/forms.ex`. A stub of that file already exists; replace it.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  Do not add or remove dependencies, and do not modify anything under\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `/home/user/catering/lib/catering/orders/` or `/home/user/catering/lib/catering/orders.ex`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  The environment is offline; everything needed is already vendored and compiled.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Every form-valued function returns an `%AshPhoenix.Form{}` struct (never a\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `%Phoenix.HTML.Form{}`), except `to_phoenix_form/1`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- The root form is named `order`: `form.name` and `form.id` are both `"order"`, so its nested\n'[39m +
                [32m'  forms are named `order[line_items][0]`, `order[line_items][0][modifiers][1]`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `order[delivery_windows][0]`, `order[customer]` and `order[fulfillment]`. A blank\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `new_order_form/0` must expose exactly the nested-form keys `:customer`, `:delivery_windows`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `:fulfillment` and `:line_items`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Every `path` argument of `add_nested`, `remove_nested`, `reorder`, `move`, `hidden_inputs` and\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `raw_error_list` is one of those full HTML names as a `String.t()`, rooted at `"order"` — for\n'[39m +
                [32m'  example `"order[line_items]"`, `"order[line_items][0][modifiers]"` or\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `"order[line_items][0][modifiers][1]"`. `"order"` itself refers to the root form. Paths at any\n'[39m +
                [32m'  depth must work.\n'[39m +
                [32m"- `new_order_form/0` builds a create form for `Catering.Orders.Order`'s `:place` action;\n"[39m +
                [32m'  `edit_order_form/1` builds an update form for the `:revise` action of the order with that id.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- The third argument of `change/3` and `add_nested/3` is a keyword list that must be forwarded\n'[39m +
                [32m'  unchanged to the underlying ash_phoenix operation; callers rely on options that hide errors,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  restrict validation to touched fields, seed the new nested form with parameters, insert it at\n'[39m +
                [32m'  the front of the list, or give it a non-default action type. Both functions must also be\n'[39m +
                [32m'  callable at the lower arity with the options defaulting to `[]`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `reorder/3` and `move/3` change the visible order **and** the order that will be submitted: the\n'[39m +
                [32m'  reordered children must appear in the new order in `submitted_params/1`, they must be renamed to\n'[39m +
                [32m'  their new indices, and `save/2` must persist the new order. `move/3` at either boundary of a list\n'[39m +
                [32m'  is a no-op.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `edit_order_form/1` must present nested children in ascending stored `position`, independently of\n'[39m +
                [32m'  the order the storage engine happens to return them in.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- Removing a nested form from an edit form and saving must destroy exactly that stored record,\n'[39m +
                [32m'  leaving unrelated records untouched.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `save/2` takes the form and either a parameter map (which must be validated into the form before\n'[39m +
                [32m'  submitting) or `nil` (submit what the form already holds). On success it returns\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `{:ok, order}` where `order` is the persisted `Catering.Orders.Order` struct with `customer`,\n'[39m +
                [32m"  `line_items` and each line item's `modifiers` already loaded, and with the line items and the\n"[39m +
                [32m'  modifiers in ascending `position`. On failure it returns `{:error, form}` where `form` is the\n'[39m +
                [32m'  re-usable `%AshPhoenix.Form{}` carrying the errors, and nothing has been written.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `hidden_inputs/2` returns a `%{String.t() => String.t()}` map: every hidden input key (including\n'[39m +
                [32m'  the form-type marker `_form_type`, the touched-field marker `_touched`, the primary key of an\n'[39m +
                [32m'  existing record, and the union member marker `_union_type`) mapped to its string value.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `error_map/1` returns a `%{String.t() => [[String.t()]]}` map, keyed by the **HTML name of the\n'[39m +
                [32m'  form that owns the errors** (`"order"`, `"order[line_items][0]"`, …). Each value is the list of\n'[39m +
                [32m"  that form's own errors as two-element lists `[field_name, message]`, sorted ascending. Forms\n"[39m +
                [32m'  without errors must be absent from the map.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `raw_error_list/2` returns the errors of the form at `path` as a list of\n'[39m +
                [32m'  `{field :: atom(), message :: String.t(), vars :: keyword()}` tuples with the message left\n'[39m +
                [32m'  untranslated (substitution variables not interpolated), sorted ascending by field name and then\n'[39m +
                [32m'  by message.\n'[39m +
                [32m'- `serialize/1` returns, for the form it is given and recursively for every nested form, a map with\n'[39m +
                [32m'  exactly these string keys:\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"name"` — the form\'s HTML name.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"id"` — the form\'s HTML id.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"type"` — `"create"`, `"update"` or `"read"`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"resource"` — the form\'s resource module rendered with `inspect/1`, e.g.\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `"Catering.Orders.LineItem"`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"valid"` — the form\'s validity as a boolean.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"hidden"` — the same map as `hidden_inputs/2` would return for this form, but **without** the\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `_touched` entry.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"values"` — a map from field name to the form\'s current value for that field, rendered with\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `to_string/1`, or `nil` when the value is `nil`. The fields are, per resource:\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `Order` → `reference`, `note`; `LineItem` → `dish`, `quantity`; `Modifier` → `label`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `surcharge_cents`; `Customer` → `name`, `email`; `DeliveryWindow` → `label`,\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `starts_at_minute`, `ends_at_minute`; `CourierDrop` → `street`, `postcode`;\n'[39m +
                [32m'    `CounterPickup` → `counter`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"errors"` — this form\'s own errors as two-element lists `[field_name, message]`, sorted\n'[39m +
                [32m'    ascending.\n'[39m +
                [32m'  - `"nested"` — a map whose keys are the string names of the nested-form keys that this form\n'[39m +
                [32m'    currently holds forms for, and whose values are the serialized child (for a single nested\n'[39m +
                [32m'    form), the list of serialized children in order (for a list of nested forms), or `nil`.'[39m
            }
          ]

                    [32m'If your action has `manage_relationship`, AshPhoenix automatically infers nested forms:\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Adding and Removing Nested Forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'</.button>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    [32m'In your LiveView:\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  {:noreply, assign(socket, :form, form)}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'end\n'[39m +

                    [32m'  </.inputs_for>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'</.form>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Manually defining nested forms\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can manually specify nested form configurations using the `forms` option.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                    [32m'AshPhoenix.Form.for_create(\n'[39m +
